 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Tennis fans criticized Naomi Osaka after the Japanese star suffered a shocking defeat to 18-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova at the Japan Open in Tokyo on Thursday.
 The seventh-seeded Osaka lost 6-3, 7-5 to the Slovakian in the second round. She initially took control by winning the first two games, but Pohankova responded strongly, winning six of the next seven games to take the first set and ultimately win the match.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Following the defeat, fans on social media criticized Osaka's performance against the world No. 144. One user questioned the effort she showed during the match:
 "It's tough to watch someone give zero effort. I wish I had the talent she had in anything in life because you know what ,I wouldn't waste it give zero effort…."
 Another user questioned whether Osaka could return to the level that helped her win four Grand Slam titles:
 "Naomi Osaka came back 3 years ago, trying to 'regain' her form … But she did, that`s the tennis and form won her grand slams but tennis has passed her and changed, simple as that … People just delusional to think she ever will win anything meaningful, she is washed, done and dusted."
 Mocking the loss, another follower wrote:
 Along similar lines, a few other fans chimed in:
 The defeat reportedly marked the end of Osaka's 2026 competitive season. However, she is expected to return to the court for exhibition events in December, including the Charlotte Invitational and The Six in Seoul.
 Naomi Osaka opened up about her loss at the Japan Open
 After her Japan Open loss, Naomi Osaka spoke to reporters about her ambitions and efforts to improve her game. Despite the disappointing result, the four-time Grand Slam champion said she remained determined to challenge for major titles.
 "Obviously, when I play a Slam, it's in my mind to challenge for it. Unfortunately, I haven't been in that position yet, and I'm going to keep attempting it. But if you're asking me how I think my tennis is, I think it's pretty good," Osaka said.
 She also discussed the outfit she wore at the Japan Open, a custom blue-and-white, crane-embroidered robe inspired by a kimono. Osaka explained that the design gave her an opportunity to express her creativity:
 "There are so many things that go on in my mind, and it was just a creative outlet. All the other sports are allowed to do that, and tennis is more subdued and restrained."
 Naomi Osaka also reflected on facing Pohankova, explaining that playing an opponent she knew little about presented a challenge. She opened the Japan Open against Jasmine Paolini and registered a 6-3, 7-6 (7-4) win against the Italian.
